newsitem.title: USA: SEC alleges insider trades at Independence Bancorp.
newsitem.headline: SEC alleges insider trades at Independence Bancorp.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday it has accused a former Independence Bancorp Inc. director and 11 other individuals with insider trading resulting in illegal profits of more than $600,000.

In a civil complaint filed in U.S. District Court in Philadelphia, the agency alleged Robert Hunter, 66, in prison for unrelated criminal charges, made illegal trades and tipped off a group of friends and relatives in the Philadelphia area about the bank holding company's pending merger with CoreStates Financial Corp.

Also named in the lawsuit were Thomas Pileggi, 52, who lives in Dresher, Pa, and W. Kenneth Greenwood, 65 of Medowbrook, Pa. Both were directors on the board of Cheltenham Bank, a subsidiary of Independence, the SEC said.
In its complaint, the SEC said Hunter not only tipped off other individuals but traded in 40,000 Independence shares himself, netting $248,250 in illegal profits.

Pileggi, a Philadelphia real estate developer, was accused by the SEC of making an illegal profit of $228,000. Greenwood, who owns a Philadelphia furniture store, was accused of making a profit of $150,412 from his illegal trades.
"Mr. Greenwood is reviewing the charges and preserving all of his options," said Greenwood's attorney, J. Shane Creamer. Pileggi and Hunter's attorneys could not be reached for comment.

The nine other defendants in the case were accused by the SEC of buying shares after being tipped off by Hunter. According to the SEC, five have settled the charges without admitting or denying any wrongdoing and have agreed to pay a total of about $80,000 in illegal profits, interest and civil penalties.
CoreStates completed its acquisition of Independence in June 1994.
